lines.text: I will sing of Your loving devotion and justice;
to You, O LORD, I will sing praises.
I will ponder the way that is blameless—
when will You come to me?
I will walk in my house
I will set no worthless thing
I hate the work of those who fall away;
it shall not cling to me.
A perverse heart shall depart from me;
I will know nothing of evil.

pictures.scene: Hendrick ter Brugghen, King David — the king leaning over his harp with the strings under his fingers, a Psalm of David
pictures.name: pd_brugghen_psalm

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, Road through an Oak Forest — a sandy track running straight in under the great oaks, I will ponder the way that is blameless
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_weg

pictures.scene: Pieter de Hooch, At the Linen Closet — the folded linen handed over in a swept hallway with the door standing open to the light, I will walk in my house
pictures.name: pd_hooch_huis

pictures.scene: Georges de La Tour, The Repentant Magdalen — the woman turned from the mirror and the jewels to the skull and the one flame, with integrity of heart
pictures.name: pd_latour_hart

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, Death and the Miser — the dying man still reaching for the money bag while Death comes in at the door, I will set no worthless thing before my eyes
pictures.name: pd_bosch_afval

pictures.scene: Duccio di Buoninsegna, The Temptation of Christ on the Mountain — Christ dismissing the devil above all the kingdoms offered to Him, I hate the work of those who fall away
pictures.name: pd_duccio_verdorven

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Joseph Accused by Potiphar's Wife — the woman beside the bed laying the charge while her husband listens, whoever slanders his neighbor in secret
